chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was a group in his presence whom he was narrating to, when a man from them mentioned a man, and he criticized him and complained of him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'And how can you find fault with your brother entirely? And which of the men is completely refined (free from faults)?'

key_terms.الْمُهَذَّبُ: the refined / the one free from faults
key_terms.فَوَقَعَ فِيهِ: criticized him / spoke ill of him

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for criticizing or complaining about others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the term 'al-muhadhdhab' (the refined/polished one) to redefine moral excellence not as sinlessness, but as the capacity to overlook others' imperfections. This hadith, found in the chapter on overlooking faults, underscores the Shia ethical ideal of social grace and patience, suggesting that true refinement lies in one's ability to forgive rather than in being flawless oneself.
